title: Saudi Arabia estimates fiscal deficit of 3.6% of GDP in 2027, finance ministry says

Total expenditure was estimated at $370.21bln and revenue projected at $319.61bln in 2027

Yomna Ehab, Ahmed Tolba and Federico Maccioni | Reuters News

Saudi Arabia has projected a fiscal deficit equivalent to 191 billion riyals ($50.87 billion) or 3.6% of gross domestic product in 2027, the finance ministry said in a pre-budget statement on Wednesday.

Total expenditure was estimated at 1.39 trillion riyals ($370.21 billion) and revenue projected at 1.20 trillion riyals ($319.61 billion) in 2027, the finance ministry said.

* The ministry estimated the 2026 deficit at 245 billion riyals, exceeding the 165 billion riyals projected in the budget published last year.

* Saudi Arabia forecast real GDP growth of 12.8% in 2027, following an expected decline of 3.6% in 2026.

* The ministry said the expected decline in real GDP in 2026 was due to a projected 21.8% drop in oil activities amid geopolitical developments in the region.

* The Iran war has led to heavy disruptions to energy shipments from the Gulf and in recent weeks Saudi Arabia has faced increasing pressure from the Iran-backed Houthis, who have fired salvos of missiles and drones at the kingdom.

* The ministry said that the 2027 deficit "will be funded through borrowing in accordance with a medium-term debt strategy framework", with the borrowing plan for the 2027 "disclosed in detail by the end of this year".

* Saudi Arabia is undertaking a massive economic overhaul known as Vision 2030, aimed at reducing reliance on oil, which requires hundreds of billions of dollars in investment.

(Reporting by Yomna Ehab, Ahmed Tolba and Federico Maccioni; Editing by Alex Richardson)
